Section(s): Kinetics analysis

Text and equations in reading order:
    In addition, the values of the specific growth rate at different initial substrate concentrations were generated for each cell line using conventional approaches. Briefly, a first-order growth was assumed to occur during the initial stage of exponential growth at each initial substrate concentration (Eq. 1).
(1) \mathbf{d}[\boldsymbol{X}]/\mathbf{d}\mathbf{t}=\mu[\boldsymbol{X}];\mathrm{~w i t h~}[\boldsymbol{X}]=[\boldsymbol{X}]_{\mathrm{o}}\circledast\mathbf{t}=\mathbf{t}_{\mathrm{o}}=0.0    [code: ODE, computes [X], code proposes balance]
    In Eq. 1, [X] is the biomass concentration at a given time, [X]₀ is the cell concentration at an initial condition, t is the time, t₀ is the initial time (corresponding to the beginning of the exponential growth phase), and μ is the specific growth rate with a constant value at least during the initial portion of the exponential phase. The integrated version of Eq. 1 renders Eq. 2, a straight-line model.
    Therefore, the value of the specific growth rate ($\mu$) was calculated from the slope of the plots of $\ln[X]$ versus $t$ at each initial substrate concentration value $[S]_{t}$. A Monod-type equation (Eq. 3) was used to fit the values of the specific growth rate ($\mu$) at different initial substrate concentrations.
(3) \mathbf{\upmu}=\mathbf{\upmu}_\mathrm{max}[\mathbf{\upS}]*/(\mathbf{K}\mathbf{s}+[\mathbf{\upS}]*);\mathrm{~with~}[\mathbf{\upS}]*=[\mathbf{\upS}]_\mathrm{o}-[\mathbf{\upS}]_\mathrm{t}    [code: algebraic, computes \mu, code proposes constitutive]
    A Lineweaver–Burk linearization was used to obtain values for the kinetic parameters: $\mu_{\mathrm{max}}$ (the maximum specific growth rate), $K_{\mathrm{s}}$ (the concentration of substrate at which half the value of $\mu_{\mathrm{max}}$ was observed), and the $[S]_{\mathrm{t}}$ (the minimum substrate concentration at which cell growth was observed). We only considered a particular linear regressions as valid if $r^{2}$ was higher than 0.97.
    The material balance for substrate consumption was assumed to be represented by Eq. 4.
(4) \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{s}}=\mathrm{d}[S]/\mathrm{d t}=\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{x}}/\mathbf{Y}_{\mathrm{x}/\mathrm{s}}    [code: ODE, computes r_{s}, code proposes balance]
    In this equation, $ r_s $ is the global rate of glucose consumption, $ r_x $ is the rate of cell growth, t is time, and $ Y_{x/s} $ is a cell yield coefficient. In agreement with Eq. 4, the yield coefficient was calculated from the slopes of $ r_x $ versus $ r_s $ plots at different $ [S]_o $ values.
    For the kinetic analysis of mAb production in shake flasks and bioreactors, the viable cell concentration profile [X] was fit to a sixth-order polynomial. The polynomial equation was derived to obtain the experimental cell production rate ( $ r_x $) at each time. A Luedeking–Piret-type model (Luedeking and Piret 1959) was proposed for the modeling of antibody production (Eq. 5).
(5) \mathbf{d}[\boldsymbol{P}]/\mathbf{d}\mathbf{t}=\mathbf{r}_{\mathbf{p}}=\alpha\mathbf{r}_{\mathbf{x}}+\boldsymbol{\beta}[\boldsymbol{X}];\quad\mathbf{r}_{\mathbf{x}}=\mathbf{d}[\boldsymbol{X}]/\mathbf{d}\mathbf{t}    [code: ODE, computes [P], code proposes balance]
    Here, [P] is the mAb concentration at a given point, t is time, $ r_p $ is the rate of accumulation of product in time within the reaction vessel, [X] is the cell concentration at that given time, $ r_x $ is the rate of cell growth, and $ \alpha $ and $ \beta $ are the Luedeking–Piret constraints.

Symbols:
  [X]: Cell concentration at a given time [cell/mL] (computed)
  \mu: Specific growth rate of the cells [h^-1] (computed)
  \mu_{max}: Maximum specific growth rate [h^-1] (parameter)
  [S]: Substrate concentration in the culture used in the Monod growth law [mg/mL] (variable)
  K: Monod saturation constant for substrate (the K in K_s) [g/L] (parameter)
  s: Subscript denoting substrate in the saturation constant K_s [-] (parameter)
  r_{s}: Global rate of glucose consumption [mg mL^-1 h^-1] (computed)
  r_{x}: Rate of cell growth [cell mL^-1 h^-1] (variable)
  Y_{x/s}: Cell yield coefficient [cell/mg] (parameter)
  [P]: mAb concentration at a given point [μg/mL] (computed)
  r_{p}: Rate of accumulation of product in time within the reaction vessel [concentration/time] (variable)
  \alpha: Luedeking–Piret constant [µg/cell] (parameter)
  \beta: Luedeking–Piret constant [µg/cell/h] (parameter)
